jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral position in probabilistic inversion of seismic data for mapping submerged landscapes and archaeological potential
jobs.description:
The Department of Geoscience, Aarhus University, Denmark, invites applications for a postdoctoral position in probabilistic inversion of seismic data, with the aim of identifying submerged landscapes and locations of archaeological potential. We are searching for a motivated and engaged researcher with experience in inversion to be part of our research team studying late Quaternary and Holocene processes and landscape evolution.

The postdoctoral position is a fixed-term full-time position for 1 year.

The postdoctoral work will be part of the international ERC Synergy Grant project SUBNORDICA, where scientists in the fields of geology, geophysics, and archaeology work together to develop methodologies for recreating submerged landscapes and human settlement in NW Europe, and for finding submerged Stone Age settlements in deeper water settings such as the North Sea. SUBNORDICA also uses machine-learning routines to identify, from existing and new data, targets of archaeological potential for more detailed investigation. The research team at the department is leading a work package focused on the eastern North Sea region. Other members in the team work on geophysical imaging methods, sea level modelling, and palaeolandscape mapping to generate palaeotopography and palaeocoastlines using both legacy and newly acquired data.

Job description
The postdoctoral position is focused on probabilistic inversion of seismic data to estimate subsurface properties that can be linked directly to the location of submerged settlements – a key example being the presence of peat, which marks former dry land.

Specific tasks will be to:

• Develop probabilistic inversion workflows for high-resolution subbottom profiles and multichannel seismic data from the North Sea, constrained by sediment core observations
• Map peat and other landscape types relevant for archaeology, and use the results together with machine-learning routines to identify targets of archaeological potential
• Provide input and constraints for predictive modelling workflows carried out at partner institutions
The postdoctoral researcher will be working closely together with post docs and senior staff in the research team at the department, as well as with the international partners in the SUBNORDICA project. Close collaboration is expected particularly with partners focused on predictive modelling for archaeology. The position provides opportunities for offshore field work and participation in joint research expeditions in the North Sea and Baltic Sea. It is also expected that the postdoc will take an active part in various research team activities and contribute to supervision and teaching of (under-) graduate students in the team.

Facilities
Laboratory facilities at the Department of Geoscience will be available for the position. This includes the acquisition, processing and interpretation facilities at SeisLab Aarhus for both multi- and single channel marine seismic and acoustic data, and an advanced sediment core laboratory.

Qualifications
The qualified applicant will have a PhD degree in geoscience, geophysics or related fields. Candidates should preferably have a background within probabilistic inversion and uncertainty quantification and/or machine learning. Experience with seismic data, including reflection seismic and hydroacoustic data, is beneficial, as is experience with linking seismic data to physical or lithological properties. Experience with the shallow subsurface of the North Sea or other similar settings, including sediment cores and marine geoarchaeology, is further beneficial but not required.

The candidate is expected to have well-documented research experience with academic publications and presentations at conferences and meetings. The applicant should also have effective organizational skills, with previous project management being beneficial. The candidate should be able to work collaboratively as part of an interdisciplinary team of geophysicists, geologists and archaeologists. Oral and written English skills are required.

Application
The application must include the following:

• Cover Letter, including motivation for applying and information on how the candidate’s qualifications and experience will aid the project
• Curriculum Vitae, including a list of publications
• PhD certificate or a statement regarding the expected date of completing of PhD studies
• One page statement of research goals
• Contact information (name, position, institution, email) for three references
We refer to the faculty’s guidelines for applicants.

Aarhus University’s goal is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to build a culture in which each employee has opportunities to thrive, advance and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Place and conditions of employment
Your place of work would be the Department of Geoscience, Høegh-Guldbergs Gade 2, DK-8000 Aarhus C, Denmark.

The Department of Geoscience prioritizes diversity and a good work environment, as this is a prerequisite for conducting progressive research. At the department, we have a diverse and international research environment, with skilled employees and access to modern and well-equipped laboratories.

Deadline
The deadline for applications is January 4, 2027. We expect to conduct interviews in mid-late January, and the selected candidate will be able to start on 1 March 2027 or as soon as possible hereafter.

Contact information
Professor Katrine Juul Andresen (katrine.andresen@geo.au.dk)

Associate Professor Thomas Mejer Hansen (tmeha@geo.au.dk)

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self. 

Formalities and salary range
Natural Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

Aarhus University also offers a Junior Researcher Development Programme targeted at career development for postdocs at AU. You can read more about it here.

At the Faculty of Natural Science at Aarhus University, we strive to support our scientific staff in their career development. We focus on competency development and career clarification and want to make your opportunities transparent. On our website, you can find information on all types of scientific positions, as well as the entry criteria we use when assessing candidates. You can also read more about how we can assist you in your career planning and development.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

jobs.occupation: Project Manager for the Construction Division at Sund & Bælt
jobs.description:
Would you like to lead regulatory, permitting and environmental projects and collaboration with German authorities?

Would you like to contribute to one of Europe’s most significant infrastructure projects: The Fehmarnbelt Project? Are you motivated by driving progress on complex regulatory, permitting and environmental compliance matters related to construction projects involving a wide range of stakeholders?

As Project Manager, you will become a key member of the Permits and Environment Germany team in the Construction Division. You will play an important role in coordinating regulatory, permitting and environmental assessments, consultants and dialogue with authorities, while acting as a link between internal project teams and external partners. This position gives you the opportunity to combine your expertise with project management and stakeholder management skills. You will have responsibility, a broad network of contacts and the opportunity to contribute to a project of major importance to societies.

The position

As Project Manager you will join Permits and Environment Germany, also known as PEG, in the Construction Division. Here, you will be responsible for leading and coordinating regulatory, permitting and environmental aspects in collaboration with internal functions, external environmental specialist-consultants, and relevant authorities involved in the construction of the Fehmarnbelt Tunnel. You will be a key point of contact on environmental matters, ensuring knowledge sharing and effective coordination across the project’s many interfaces. Your collaborators will include:

• Colleagues in Permits and Environment Germany

• Internal project teams and technical functions

• External environmental and specialist consultants

• German authorities and other external stakeholders

• The project organization and contractors

Your main place of work can be based at one of our offices in Copenhagen, Rødbyhavn or Burg, depending on your preference and agreement, with the possibility of also working from Hamburg. The role involves collaboration across locations, including regular visits to our other offices and meetings with authorities in northern Germany.

Depending on your place of employment, you will be offered either a German or Danish employment contract.

Responsibilities

You will have a varied role, ensuring progress on specific deliverables while bringing together different regulatory, permitting and environmental disciplines and project interests. A key part of your work will involve delegating tasks to external consultants and following up on their work, as well as ensuring that environmental requirements are addressed promptly and professionally.

• Lead and coordinate external environmental and specialist consultants and their deliverables

• Plan, commission and follow up on regulatory, permitting and environmental assessments

• Coordinate regulatory, permitting and environmental matters with the relevant German authorities

• Support internal functions with regulatory, permitting and environmental advice and knowledge sharing

• Coordinate the project’s regulatory, permitting and environmental interfaces between internal teams, consultants, contracts and other stakeholders

Your background

You hold a relevant higher education qualification in a field such as landscape or environmental planning, geography, biology, environmental science, political science, public administration or - management or a related discipline.

You have experience in project management and maybe also in coordinating external consultants. You have a basic understanding of German nature conservation and environmental legislation, along with experience in communicating and coordinating with German authorities. You are fluent in written and spoken German and English and communicate clearly and professionally.

Experience in environmental supervision on construction projects, including Umweltbaubegleitung (UBB), would be an advantage, as would experience with environmental matters in major construction, civil engineering or marine projects, German planning approval and plan amendment procedures, and compliance with environmental requirements during construction.

You as a person

You work in a structured and independent manner and take responsibility for moving your tasks forward. You thrive in a role involving many stakeholders and build trusting relationships through clear and approachable communication.

• You are responsible and reliable, and see your tasks through to completion

• You take a proactive, solution-oriented approach

• You maintain an overview of complex projects

• You are flexible and able to adapt to changing needs and priorities

• You contribute actively to collaboration and the professional community

About the Fehmarnbelt Project

You will be part of a dedicated and international organisation and part of one of Europe’s largest infrastructure projects; the Fehmarnbelt Tunnel. As part of Sund & Bælt, you join a wider organisation with opportunities to collaborate, develop and contribute beyond the Fehmarnbelt project**.** We offer an open and informal work environment, responsibility, and the opportunity to make a difference through work that matters to society.

The Fehmarnbelt Project is one of Europe’s largest infrastructure projects, creating a new 18 km fixed link between Denmark and Germany. With major construction activities underway both at sea and on land, the project brings together specialists and expertise from across countries and disciplines. The project is part of Sund & Bælt’s portfolio of major infrastructure projects and will strengthen the connection between Denmark, Germany and the rest of Europe. For more information about the project, please visit www.femern.de.

Interested?

We aim to be an inclusive workplace that embraces diversity. We therefore encourage everyone to apply, regardless of gender, age, ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation or disability.

jobs.occupation: Risk Managers for large-scale infrastructure projects at Sund & Bælt
jobs.description:
Turn uncertainty into better infrastructure decisions

Would you like to help shape decisions on some of Denmark's largest and most important infrastructure projects?

At Sund & Bælt, we develop, construct and operate infrastructure that matters to society. We are looking for Risk Managers to strengthen our Risk Management team within the Project Service Organisation. We welcome candidates at different levels of experience. Your curiosity, analytical ability, willingness to learn and capacity to create impact matter more than prior knowledge of specific risk management systems.

You will support projects across our portfolio and throughout the project lifecycle, including the Fehmarn Belt project, our Major Projects portfolio and future large-scale infrastructure initiatives such as Østlig Ringvej and Copenhagen storm surge protection. Working on the owner's side, you will help us understand and manage the risks and opportunities associated with complex projects. Your insights will enable project leaders to act at the right time and make well-informed decisions about project delivery, contingency and risk responses. You will join a small team of currently one Risk Managers led by the Head of Risk Management. The team works closely together, shares experience and provides a strong professional environment for learning and continuous improvement.

The role

As a Risk Manager, you will help Sund & Bælt understand and manage its exposure as an infrastructure owner. Embedded in our projects, you will work closely with project teams and specialists to challenge delivery assumptions, assess cost and schedule uncertainty, and translate complex analysis into practical recommendations.

You will support assigned projects according to portfolio needs and your experience. At the same time, you will contribute to a consistent professional approach to risk management across our project portfolio and the full project lifecycle. This includes using AI in our work and helping implement practical AI initiatives that strengthen risk identification, analysis, reporting and decision support across the project portfolio. Project managers and designated risk owners remain accountable for their risks and responses. Your role is to provide specialist expertise, independent challenge and practical follow-through.

• Work closely with project managers, risk owners and colleagues in planning, finance, cost control, engineering, construction, commercial, legal and operational functions.

• Support decisions throughout the project lifecycle, from feasibility studies and procurement to execution and commissioning.

• Provide independent and constructive challenge while maintaining clear roles and accountability.

• Help strengthen owner-side risk management across a diverse infrastructure portfolio.

• Contribute to the development of professional methods, tools and data quality, including the implementation and responsible use of AI within risk management, and support organisational learning.

Responsibilities

Your work will help turn threats, opportunities and uncertainty into decision-relevant insight. You will examine what could affect delivery, identify the most important drivers of exposure and help project teams define realistic and effective responses. You will:

• Prepare and facilitate multidisciplinary risk reviews and workshops to identify threats, opportunities, dependencies and interfaces, and test the assumptions behind project delivery.

• Develop qualitative assessments and contribute to quantitative cost and schedule risk analyses, critically examining input quality, ranges, dependencies, sensitivities and the implications of the results.

• Connect risk insight with estimates, schedules, forecasts and change assessments in collaboration with planning, finance, commercial and project controls colleagues.

• Assess Sund & Bælt's retained and interface exposure across approvals, procurement, contractors, construction and operational readiness, working with relevant specialists.

• Maintain decision-relevant risk registers and follow up on response actions. Assess whether actions are feasible and effective, track residual exposure and raise material concerns at the appropriate time.

• Prepare clear analyses and recommendations for project decisions, identify common drivers across projects, and contribute to improved methods, tools and organisational learning. Help develop, test and implement AI-supported risk management approaches across the project portfolio.

Your background

We welcome candidates at different stages of their careers and value strong analytical thinking, sound judgement, and the potential to grow and make an impact. We are looking for:

• A relevant educational background, for example in engineering, construction management, economics, or equivalent practical experience.

• Strong numerical and analytical skills, attention to data quality, and the ability to distinguish evidence from assumptions.

• Clear communication skills and the ability to work constructively across disciplines.

• Strong written and spoken English. Danish is also widely used in the organisation.

• Confidence using Excel and an interest in applying risk management, analytical and AI-enabled tools.

• Experience with infrastructure and construction is an advantage.

You as a person

You combine analytical rigour with practical judgement. You are curious about causes, dependencies and data quality, and you distinguish clearly between evidence, assumptions and false precision. You build trust across technical, commercial and management disciplines and are comfortable asking difficult questions constructively.

• Maintain independent judgement while collaborating closely with project teams and risk owners.

• Communicate complex issues clearly and adapt your recommendations to the audience and the decision at hand.

• Take ownership, follow through on commitments and escalate material concerns at the right time.

• Work pragmatically with incomplete information without compromising professional rigour.

• Focus on improving project delivery rather than producing risk reports for their own sake.

What do we offer?

At Sund & Bælt, you will become part of an international workplace where skilled colleagues succeed together. There is room for flexibility, new ideas and opportunities to develop, both professionally and personally. You will be given responsibility and the opportunity to make a difference through work that matters to society. In addition, we offer:

• Health and dental insurance.

• A salary package based on your qualifications.

• A pension scheme.

• A canteen scheme.

Are you interested?

We want to be an inclusive workplace that embraces diversity.

We encourage everyone to apply, regardless of gender, age, ethnicity, religion, sexual orientation or disability.

Submit your CV by the application deadline, 03/01/2027 using the link below.

As Sund & Bælt manages critical infrastructure, security clearance is a condition of employment. Further information will be provided later in the recruitment process.

If you have any questions, you are welcome to contact Head of Risk Management Mads Ole Aaris on +45 28 19 79 89.

You can find more information about Sund & Bælt at www.sundogbaelt.dk.

We look forward to hearing from you.

jobs.description:
We are extra[not]ordinary

*(ex· tra· not· or· di· nary |\ ik-ˈstr-not-ȯr-də-ˌner-ē)

Adjective: A unique word for Genmab meaning to go way beyond what is

usual; to be remarkable; proudly unique and authentic

JOB DESCRIPTION

At Genmab, we are dedicated to building extra[not]ordinary® futures, together, by developing antibody products and groundbreaking, knock-your-socks-off KYSO antibody medicines® that change lives and the future of cancer treatment and serious diseases. We strive to create, champion and maintain a global workplace where individuals’ unique contributions are valued and drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our patients, care partners, families and employees.

Our people are compassionate, candid, and purposeful, and our business is innovative and rooted in science. We believe that being proudly authentic and determined to be our best is essential to fulfilling our purpose. Yes, our work is incredibly serious and impactful, but we have big ambitions, bring a ton of care to pursuing them, and have a lot of fun while doing so.

Does this inspire you and feel like a fit? Then we would love to have you join us!

The Role

Genmab is looking for a dedicated Manager to take responsibility for GMP equipment qualification and validation at our new manual clinical secondary packaging and labelling facility in Ballerup.

You will be part of a small, agile team supporting clinical trials, helping ensure that high-quality investigational medicinal products reach patients globally with cancer and other serious diseases on time and in full.

As Genmab’s newly established in-house GMP production capability for secondary packaging and labelling, the facility offers a unique opportunity to help establish equipment, processes and ways of working from the beginning. You will play a key role in ensuring that equipment is fit for its intended use, appropriately qualified and maintained in a qualified state throughout its lifecycle.

This is a position with responsibility for leading activities and coordinating stakeholders within your area of expertise. The role does not include line management or direct reports.

The position is based at our Ballerup site and requires on-site presence. You will report to the Associate Director, Team Lead, Global Clinical Supply, based in Ballerup.

Responsibilities

The role combines technical ownership, hands-on qualification activities, GMP documentation and hands-on production work in our manual packaging and labelling operations. Working closely with colleagues in Global Clinical Supply, operations, Quality Assurance, Facility and external suppliers, you will drive activities from defining requirements and planning qualifications through execution, reporting and ongoing lifecycle management.

• Own and coordinate qualification and validation activities for GMP equipment supporting clinical packaging, labelling and storage, ensuring that scope, documentation and testing reflect intended use and identified risks.

• Develop and maintain qualification strategies, plans, risk assessments, User Requirements Specifications and qualification documentation, including protocols and reports for Design, Installation, Operational and Performance Qualification, as applicable.

• Coordinate supplier deliverables and review technical documentation to ensure that equipment and supporting documentation meet defined requirements.

• Take responsibility for temperature mapping and qualification of temperature-controlled storage equipment, including associated monitoring and alarm functions, in collaboration with relevant stakeholders.

• Establish and maintain the qualified state of equipment through periodic reviews, requalification and assessment of changes, maintenance and calibration activities.

• Lead investigations and resolution of deviations arising during qualification and validation and manage related change controls and CAPAs in collaboration with Quality Assurance and equipment users.

• Develop and maintain SOPs, work instructions and equipment lifecycle documentation, ensuring clear responsibilities and practical, compliant routines.

• Contribute to inspection and audit readiness by maintaining complete, traceable documentation and presenting activities within your area of responsibility.

• Drive practical improvements that strengthen equipment reliability, documentation quality and efficient execution of qualification and validation activities.

• Perform hands-on secondary packaging and labelling activities for clinical trials in accordance with approved procedures, batch documentation and GMP, including manual set-up and operation, in-process checks, reconciliation of materials and labels, and timely, accurate completion of batch documentation and logbooks.

As part of a small team, you will also participate in day-to-day secondary packaging and labelling activities for clinical trials. This is an expected part of the role, with the balance between qualification activities and production work varying according to operational needs. Flexibility and a willingness to contribute across tasks are essential to ensuring timely clinical supplies.

Qualifications

• A relevant degree in engineering, pharmaceutical sciences, natural sciences or a related technical field, or equivalent qualifications supported by substantial relevant experience.

• Five or more years of relevant experience in a GMP-regulated environment, including independent responsibility for equipment qualification and validation.

• Demonstrated experience planning, documenting and executing qualification activities, including risk assessments, requirements specifications, test protocols and reports.

• A solid understanding of GMP requirements, equipment lifecycle principles, data integrity and risk-based qualification approaches.

• Experience with deviations, change controls, CAPAs and technical investigations.

• Ability to translate technical and operational requirements into clear, testable acceptance criteria and robust documentation.

• Experience working with equipment suppliers and coordinating activities across operations and Quality Assurance.

• Experience with packaging and labelling equipment e.g. Label printers, refrigerators, temperature-controlled storage or monitoring systems is an advantage.

• Experience establishing new equipment or working in a facility start-up environment is considered a plus.

• Hands-on experience with GMP production, ideally secondary packaging and labelling, is an advantage, together with a willingness to complete the training required to perform these activities.

• Proficient in English (written and spoken); Danish is an advantage.

• Good IT skills and willingness to learn new digital tools and systems.

About You

You are a structured and technically curious professional who enjoys taking ownership from initial requirements to completed qualifications and ongoing operation. You combine attention to detail with sound judgment and a practical approach to solving problems.

You are comfortable leading activities through your expertise, building alignment across functions and following up on commitments. You communicate clearly, challenge assumptions constructively and ensure that decisions and conclusions are supported by appropriate documentation.

You thrive in a small team where collaboration and flexibility are essential. You enjoy working close to equipment and operations, and you are motivated by building reliable, practical ways of working in an evolving environment. You can balance changing priorities while maintaining a clear focus on quality, compliance and patient needs.

The Team

jobs.occupation: Postdoc in Statistical learning as a tool to understand host-microbiome-flavour interactions in plant growth
jobs.description:
We are looking for a highly motivated and dynamic postdoc for a two-year position at the University of Copenhagen, as part of the ongoing Novo Nordisk Foundation funded project ‘Tomatoponics’. The goal of the project is to apply statistical and machine learning tools to multi-omics data including plant genotypes, root microbiomes and fruit shotgun metabolomes to better understand how the host and microbiome affect the fruit flavour. We aim to go beyond genotype-phenotype associations to reveal causal pathways, that will be tested in future trials.

  The candidate will be principally advised by Assoc. Prof. Shyam Gopalakrishnan, who leads the FindingPheno project based at the Center for Evolutionary Hologenomics (https://ceh.ku.dk), with additional guidance from Prof Tom Gilbert, Director of the Center. The Gopalakrishnan research group focuses on using population and statistical genetics to understand genotype-phenotype associations with a special focus on the role of microbiomes in evolutionary processes.

  Information on the department can be found at https://globe.ku.dk.

  Your job

  You will analyse a pre-generated dataset consisting of root metagenomes, resequenced plant genomes, untargeted fruit metabolomes plus other phenotypic data from a dataset of 10 cultivars exposed to 4 different microbiome treatments. The first part of the project will focus on performing exploratory analyses to understand the relationship between host genomic processes and microbiome variations that have a significant impact on the plant fruit chemistry and other phenotypes, with a particular focus on host-microbiome interactions. Subsequently, statistical and machine learning models will be applied to better understand the biological mechanisms and pathways involved, to help design a second trial aimed at testing predictions generated from the data.

  Our research

  As part of the projects, the postdoctoral fellow will collaborate with the wider team, that additionally includes researchers at the Department of Food Science (UCPH), Aarhus University and Aalborg University. The candidate will also have an opportunity to interact with the tomato industry, such as Danish based growers. Thus, teamwork and collaboration will be important skills; however, the candidate will also be given ownership over their own research project and deliverables.

  The fully funded postdoctoral fellowship will be hosted at the Section for Hologenomics/Center for Evolutionary Hologenomics at the GLOBE Institute. As such the candidate will also have the opportunity to collaborate with leaders in the fields of world leading experts in population genetics, statistical genetics, computational biology, clinical microbiology, archaeology, evolutionary genomics, and many other related fields of research. The University of Copenhagen is a world-leading institution of higher learning and provides excellent programs in genetics, archaeology, statistics, computer science and mathematics.

  Profile 
 We are looking for a highly motivated and enthusiastic scientist with the following competencies and experience:

  Essential experience and skills:

   	
• PhD degree or equivalent doctorate, with a background in one or more of the following areas: statistics, data science, statistical genetics, computational biology, bioinformatics, computer science, and/or mathematics 	
• Demonstrated working proficiency in one or more programming languages commonly used in data science (e.g. Python, R, C/C++, Java or Julia) 	
• Experience working in the UNIX operating environment 	
• Excellent English skills written and spoken   Desirable experience and skills:

   	
• Previous experience or strong interest in working with large scale biological data such as genomics, metagenomics, multi-omics, etc. 	
• Experience with high-performance computing clusters/systems 	
• Experience with compiling and working with data from different sources 	
• Understanding of FAIR data principles, interest in Open Data 	
• Interest in scientific communication and/or public outreach   Place of employment

  The place of employment is at the Section for Hologenomics, Oester Farimagsgade 5, 1353 Copenhagen C.

  About Globe Institute
 The Globe Institute is part of the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences at the University of Copenhagen. The Institute’s main purpose is to address basic scientific questions through interdisciplinary approaches. The institute operates at the intersection of natural and medical sciences and the humanities. Information on the institute can be found at: http://www.globe.ku.dk/.

  The Globe Institute is committed to creating an inclusive and diverse environment where employees and students can belong and thrive. See website for more information. All qualified applicants will receive full consideration. Candidates who, through their research, teaching, and/or service, contribute to diversity and competencies of our Institute are encouraged to apply. The University of Copenhagen strives to offer a family friendly and flexible working environment with a sustainable balance between work- and private life, including parental leave schemes (up to 47 weeks for both parents) and up to six weeks of paid holidays per year. Researchers that have not been tax liable in Denmark for the last 10 years can apply for a special (reduced) tax scheme. The university offers a variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families.

  Terms of employment 
 The average weekly working hours are 37 hours per week.

  The psoition is a fixed-term position limited to a period of 2 years. The starting date is on 1st of April 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The position is covered by the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff.

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State.

  Negotiation for salary supplement is possible.

  You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

  The application, in English, must be submitted electronically by clicking APPLY NOW below.

  Questions
 For further information please contact Assoc. Prof. Shyam Gopalakrishnan: shyam.gopalakrishnan@sund.ku.dk  and/or Prof. Tom Gilbert: tgilbert@sund.ku.dk .

  Foreign applicants may find this link useful: www.ism.ku.dk (International Staff Mobility).

  Application procedure
 Your online application must be submitted in English by clicking ‘Apply now’ below. Furthermore, your application must include the following documents/attachments – all in PDF format:

   	
• Motivated letter of application (max. one page). 	
• CV incl. education, work/research experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position. 	
• A certified/signed copy of a) PhD certificate and b) Master of Science certificate. If the PhD is not completed, a written statement from the supervisor will do. 	
• List of publications.   Deadline for applications: 17 January 2027, 23.59pm CET.

  The further process 
 After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the hiring committee. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment by an unbiased assessor. Once the assessment work has been completed each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself.
